scenario.briefing: A campus service reads port values from small config lines. Bad input must be reported as absent, not crash the process.

accessibility.summary: The Kotlin workspace is keyboard accessible. Checks verify source structure; they do not compile or run Kotlin.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use Tab to move between the editor and results. Ctrl+Enter runs the checks.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each check announces its description, whether it passed, and the missing or forbidden source fragment.

title: Validate configuration without exceptions
summary: Turn malformed port text into null instead of an exception, then diagnose a fallback that hides bad configuration.

objectives.description: Parse a boundary value without throwing.
Diagnose an exception used for ordinary input.
Apply the accepted range to a new config line.

hints: substringAfter with a missing delimiter returns the whole string, so pass a default.
toIntOrNull returns null instead of throwing.
Return the parsed value only when it is in range.

misconceptions.description: Using toInt and letting malformed input throw.
misconceptions.testDescription: Invalid text and out-of-range ports become null.
misconceptions.feedback: Malformed config is ordinary input, not an exceptional program state. toIntOrNull makes the failure a value the caller must handle.

misconceptions.description: Catching the parse failure and returning a sentinel port.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Catching NumberFormatException and returning -1 so the service starts with a bad port.
misconceptions.feedback: A sentinel travels through the service and fails later. Return null or a typed result so the caller decides.

misconceptions.description: Treating a parse failure as port zero.
misconceptions.feedback: Port zero is not a valid listening port. A silent fallback moves the failure away from the bad line.

misconceptions.description: Accepting zero because the integer parsed successfully.
misconceptions.feedback: Parsing succeeded, but zero is outside the accepted 1..65535 range. Validate the meaning after parsing the syntax.

sections.title: Parse, then validate
sections.body: String.toInt() throws NumberFormatException when the text is not an integer. String.toIntOrNull() returns Int? instead, which keeps malformed input in the ordinary return path. After parsing, check the meaning: a TCP port is valid only from 1 through 65535. The two failures are different, but both can be represented as null when the caller only needs a usable port.

sections.title: Exceptions are for exceptional boundaries
sections.body: Kotlin exceptions are unchecked. require(condition) { message } throws IllegalArgumentException, check throws IllegalStateException, and runCatching wraps a throw in a Result. Use exceptions when the caller cannot continue and a null when absence is an expected answer. Do not catch an exception only to return a magic number.

sections.title: Small functions are testable
sections.body: A pure function such as parsePort(line: String): Int? can be tested with kotlin.test assertions and a table of boundary inputs: valid, zero, 65535, 65536, and text. Gradle runs the suite with ./gradlew test, while kotlinc compiles a standalone file for a quick check.

steps.title: Parse a port line
steps.prompt: Edit Main.kt. parsePort returns the port when the line contains an integer from 1 through 65535, and null otherwise.
hints: Read the value after port= and trim surrounding space.
Return null when the conversion fails.
Check the accepted range before returning.

localVerification.description: Compiles the file with kotlinc and runs it, so a malformed line would throw if toInt were still used.

tests.description: The function keeps a nullable Int result.
Invalid text and out-of-range ports become null.

steps.title: The silent sentinel
steps.prompt: The service starts on a bad port after a malformed line. Select the faulty instruction and the correct repair.
hints: The parse itself is where malformed text becomes an exception.
A fallback of zero is still a port the service may try to bind.
The caller needs absence, not a magic value.
Use toIntOrNull and return null on failure.

fixes.label: Use raw.toIntOrNull() and return null when it is null.
Catch NumberFormatException and rethrow it unchanged.

steps.explanation: runCatching with getOrDefault(0) erases the failure and hands the service an invalid port. toIntOrNull keeps the failure visible, and the range check rejects zero as well.

steps.title: The zero boundary
steps.prompt: A config line reads port=0. parsePort accepts only 1 through 65535. What should it return?
hints: The text is a valid integer, so this is not a parse failure.
Zero cannot be a listening port here.
Return null because no valid port exists.

quiz.prompt: A config line reads port=0. parsePort accepts only 1 through 65535. What should it return?
quiz.explanation: Zero parses as an integer but is outside the accepted port range. Returning null represents the absence of a usable port, while substituting 65535 invents a value.
